text:
devon: Heads-up — we’re seeing a weird packing pattern in us-west2: lots of pods grabbing 1 GPU but landing on multi-GPU nodes leaving 3-7 GPUs idle on those nodes.

maria: Ugh. Is this after the device-plugin upgrade yesterday?

devon: Might be related. Quick snapshot:
```
NODE           GPU_TOTAL GPU_USED PODS
gpu-node-a     8         1       5 x small-gpu-job
gpu-node-b     8         6       3 x batch-train
gpu-node-c     4         1       8 x tiny-infer
```
Looks like tiny jobs are scattering instead of packing.

anya: Do those pods use strict podAntiAffinity or topologySpread?

devon: Yes — we added a strict anti-affinity for tiny-infer last week to avoid co-locating same-team jobs. It was intended for tenancy but now it's fragmenting pools.

sam: Also seeing scheduler/kubelet mismatch in logs. Snippet: 
```
I0310 10:22:12 scheduler: Binding pod tiny-infer-xyz -> gpu-node-a
I0310 10:22:13 kubelet: Pod tiny-infer-xyz admitted
I0310 10:22:14 device-plugin: allocation request rejected: resourceName mismatch (expected nvidia.com/gpu, got gpu.com/slot)
I0310 10:22:15 kubelet: Evicting pod tiny-infer-xyz: device plugin failed allocation
```
That allocate->evict loop leaves a hole — scheduler thinks slot consumed briefly, then freed but placement decisions already made.

liu: Wait — didn't we roll device-plugin v0.6 that introduced vendor-specific resource alias gpu.com/slot in annotations? If scheduler predicates use nvidia.com/gpu but kubelet uses gpu.com/slot, allocation can fail.

devon: Confirmed — dp rollout yesterday had a config toggle defaulting to gpu.com/slot. Some older nodes still advertise nvidia.com/gpu. Mixed resource names across nodes.

maria: Cost impact quick check: idle-GPU-minutes spiked ~22% in us-west2 over the last 12h. Rough estimate ~= $4k/day extra if sustained.

infra-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-0427 — "latebind allocation mismatch causing GPU fragmentation" (priority: high)

anya: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) relax anti-affinity for tiny-infer (allow packing), 2) enforce consistent resourceName on device-plugin via daemonset rollback, 3) scheduler tweak to prefer binpack for small-gpu classes.

devon: I can open a rollback PR for dp and run a clustered daemonset with resourceName=nvidia.com/gpu. Also will add a one-off job to cordon + drain the most fragmented nodes and reschedule.

sam: I’ll prepare a scheduler canary change to bias scoring towards packing for pod size <2 GPUs — deploy to canary pool in 10m. If it reduces fragmentation we keep, otherwise revert.

liu: Also add a node label check in the admission webhook to fail early if resource names mismatch — prevents bind/evict churn.

maria: Agree. Who owns the rollback? @sam @devon? Need quick cost gating if this hits prod.

devon: I’ll own dp rollback and the drain job. Sam will do scheduler canary. Posting updates here as they happen.

sam: Starting canary rollout now — will post status.

kube-bot: Pod eviction sweep queued on gpu-node-a (reason: device-plugin allocation failure)

devon: Rolling out dp rollback to 20% of nodes (canary), forcing resourceName=nvidia.com/gpu. Will monitor idle-GPU-minutes.

maria: Nice. If we get immediate improvement, we should backfill scale-down to reclaim completely idle nodes.

sam: Canary result after 15m: packing score improved, idle-GPU-minutes down ~9% in canary AZ. Rolling to 50%.

devon: Reverted bad dp config on canary nodes and scheduled drain for the top 8 most fragmented nodes. Will follow up with PR to unify resource names across fleets and add admission checks.

maria: Thanks — keep cost numbers in the incident doc.

devon: Will do.

sam: Patch merged to scheduler: preferBinpackForSmallPods=true (canary). Will monitor for side effects.

maria: FYI — please also notify customer success if this affects any dedicated clusters. Might need to coordinate maintenance windows.

devon: Noted, pinging @cs-team.

sam: Update 30m: fragmentation metric trending down in the canary region, no regressions observed. Moving to full rollout in 1h unless objections.

anya: No objections from infra side. After rollout, follow-up items: admission webhook, tight integration tests for dp resourceName, and a small-postmortem explaining the config drift.

devon: Thanks all. I'll file the postmortem and link in INF-2026-0427.
